info.title: Pithy
info.description: Every HTTP route the Pithy kit ships, each tagged with the capability that mounts it, as composed for `prod`. A Worker serves the routes of the capabilities it composes; `pithy contract` writes that Worker's own document. Generated by packages/cli/src/openapi/writeKitDocument.ts. Do not edit by hand; run `bun run kit-contract`.

get.summary: Report liveness, and which build is answering.

200.description: Liveness, and which build is answering.

status.description: Always `ok`: an answer at all is the liveness signal.

version.description: The Cloudflare version id of the build answering, or null where the Worker cannot say.

schema.description: Liveness, and which build is answering.

get.summary: Prove the connection and the key it signs with.

200.description: Connectivity, and proof of which key answered.

status.description: Always `ok`. A failure is an error payload, never this shape.

connectionId.description: The connection this call authenticated as.

environment.description: The environment that connection is bound to.

keyId.description: The key that verified this call. The proof a newly registered key works.

now.description: This Worker's clock, ISO-8601 — what a token's lifetime is judged against.

schema.description: Connectivity, and proof of which key answered.

get.summary: Describe what this Worker composes and how to call its admin surface.

200.description: What this Worker is, what it composes, and how to call the admin surface it exposes.

environment.description: The environment this connection is bound to, echoed so a client can label what it is looking at.

connectionId.description: The connection this call authenticated as.

version.description: The Cloudflare version id of the build answering this call, from the `CF_VERSION_METADATA` binding, or null where the binding is absent. Opaque and per-deploy: it identifies which build is running, never which features it has. Null is honest — a Worker scaffolded before the binding was declared genuinely cannot say.

versionCreatedAt.description: When the version answering this call was uploaded, ISO-8601, from the same `CF_VERSION_METADATA` binding as `version` — or null where the binding is absent. The id alone cannot tell a deploy from a rollback: a rollback reactivates an existing version, so the id returns to one already seen while this moves backwards. Relayed, never interpreted. Absent from a Worker older than #132.

privacy.description: What this project declares about privacy and what its running code holds: classes and counts, never field names (`GET /control-plane/privacy` has those, behind `privacy:read`). Present on every Worker from #132, `declared` explicitly empty when nothing was declared; absent from an older Worker.

items.description: A class name.

declared.description: The classes the project declared, as attested by the last `pithy deploy`. Empty when it declared none; null when no attestation reached this Worker.

items.description: A class name.

observed.description: Every class with at least one marked field in this Worker's storage schemas, derived at runtime. Null when the project declared no class, because nothing was walked.

counts.description: Marked fields per observed class. A class with none is absent rather than zero. Null when nothing was walked.

items.description: A class name.

observedNotDeclared.description: Classes the code holds that the project never declared — a posture change nobody escalated. Null when nothing was walked.

items.description: A class name.

declaredNotObserved.description: Classes declared with no marked field behind them — an unfinished migration. Null when nothing was walked.

consoleGate.description: The console gate, as last attested.

consoleGateReason.description: Why the gate is `unverifiable`, in one sentence. Null otherwise.

attestedAt.description: When the attestation was written, ISO-8601, or null when there is none. A version created long after it is a build the attestation does not describe.

items.description: A storage kind: `d1` tables, or `kv` stores.

sources.description: The storage the observed classes were derived from. Anything not listed was not walked; empty when nothing was.

retirement.description: The field key's retirement guard (#390): whether a version due to leave is held live, and by what. Absent on a Worker whose core predates encrypted fields.

blocked.description: Whether a version due to leave the window is being held live by one of `reasons`.

items.description: `unrotatable` — an encrypted field rests outside D1, so nothing can prove it re-sealed. `incomplete-coverage` — a schema source the guard derives from was not read. `stale` — a row still holds an envelope or an index under a version due to leave.

reasons.description: Every reason the guard is not clean now, empty when it is. Read directly: never inferred.

liveVersions.description: How many field-key versions are live. Two is the normal state: current and previous.

items.description: One capability this Worker composes, as reported to one caller: its version, its admin surface, and the summary that caller is entitled to — or the named reason there is none.

name.description: The capability's name — the same token used as its migration namespace and error domain.

version.description: The npm version of the package supplying this capability, or null where there is none — the adopter's own `app` capability has a name and no package. Reported per capability and never aggregated: a project composes some capabilities and not others, so only the intersection of what it composes and what changed is worth reporting. Joined against a release feed on the `package` beside it, never on `name` — the two are different kinds of thing.

package.description: The npm package supplying this capability — the join key against a release feed — or null where there is none, which is the adopter's own `app` capability and a Worker that predates this field. **Never derivable from `name`:** `controlplane` ships inside `@pithy-sh/core`, so a name-derived `@pithy-sh/<name>` reaches a package that has never been published and the join comes back empty, which reads exactly like up to date. Null together with `version`: a package with no version says nothing joinable, and a version with no package is the reason this field exists.

method.description: The method to call this route with.

path.description: The **fully mounted** path, with the capability's configured `basePath` already applied — `/billing/entitlements/grant`, not `/entitlements/grant`. Built by the capability at assembly, so an adopter who moved the mount point is reflected here rather than silently breaking a client that assumed the default.

anyOf.description: One management operation a connection may perform, as a colon-separated `resource:action` code. The taxonomy is federated: each capability declares its own scopes, and core holds only the seam's.

scope.description: The scope this route requires, or null when it needs only a verified caller (the seam's `ping`). A client compares it against the connection's granted scopes to know which operations it may actually offer, instead of discovering a 403 by trying.

summary.description: One line describing what the route does, for a management client to render beside it.

items.description: One admin route, described well enough for a management client to call it without holding any capability-specific knowledge.

adminRoutes.description: Every admin route this capability contributes, or empty when it contributes none. Most capabilities are empty: having no management surface is the normal case, and saying so explicitly is what lets a client render a capability it cannot act on.

healthKeys.description: The closed vocabulary of scalars this capability may report about its own state, or empty when it reports none — including when the Worker predates this field and says nothing at all. Declared alongside the routes so a client can render a key it has never heard of from what the Worker says about it — and so a *withheld* number is visible as a key with no value, rather than as silence.

key.description: The key this value appears under in the capability's summary. One camelCase token.

kind.description: Whether the value is a count or a member of a closed list.

states.description: Every value a `state` key may take, so a client can render each one it knows and nothing for one it does not. Null for a `count`, and required for a `state`: an enum with no members is a string field wearing a costume.

scope.description: The scope this value is behind — one the capability's own admin routes already require, never a new one. A caller without it gets no value rather than a zero.

cost.description: What producing this value costs on a manifest read.

summary.description: One line saying what the number means, for a client to render beside it without knowing the key.

nominal.description: What a nominal value is for this key — a bound for a `count`, the nominal members for a `state`, or null where the capability makes no claim. A client reads null as `unknowable`, never as healthy.

atMost.description: The largest nominal value, inclusive. Above it the value wants attention.

atLeast.description: The smallest nominal value, inclusive. Below it the value wants attention.

anyOf.description: A count's nominal range: at least one bound, inclusive at its edge. Neither is a claim with no content; an inverted pair is one nothing can satisfy.

items.description: One bounded scalar a capability contributes to its manifest entry: what it is called, what it may be, what it costs, and which scope it is behind.

configKeys.description: The configured facts this capability states, or empty when it states none — including when the Worker predates this field. Declared alongside the routes, because a fact is what a client needs to *call* one: `POST /billing/entitlements/grant` names a holder and never assumes it, so a client that cannot learn what this project bills can only guess — and a guess writes a row nothing reads.

key.description: The key this fact appears under in the capability's config. One camelCase token.

choices.description: Every value this fact may take, so a client can offer the same choice the adopter made, or null where the values are not enumerable. At least one where it is a list: an empty one is not `null` spelled differently, it is a list nothing satisfies, so the capability could never boot and the refusal would name no permitted value at all. Read off the capability's own enum rather than retyped, so a new member cannot land without the manifest learning it.

summary.description: One line saying what the fact governs, for a client to render beside it without knowing the key.

items.description: One configured fact a capability states: what it is called, what it may be, and what it decides — enough for a client to respect a decision it did not make.

config.description: What each declared fact resolved to for this deployment. The same answer for every caller, read off the capability's parsed config at assembly: there is no producer here, so no failure state, no per-request cost, and no staleness beyond the manifest itself.

additionalProperties.description: One scalar: a word, a number, or a flag. Nothing else is representable — no nested objects, no lists, no credentials.

health.description: Every declared value this caller may see, or null when there is none to give — either nothing is declared, or this connection lacks the scope the value is behind, or producing it failed, or the Worker predates this field. **Null is never zero.**

additionalProperties.description: One scalar: a number, or a member of the closed list its key declares. Nothing else is representable — no names, no ids, no rows, no nested objects.

anyOf.description: One capability's health summary: each declared key to its scalar. Unknown keys parse rather than throw, so a client of an older build renders what it knows and nothing for the rest.

healthUnavailable.description: Whether producing this capability's summary failed on this read — the fourth state (#350), and the reason `health` being null is not enough on its own. Carries no message, no code and no error: what the producer threw may name a row or a key, so nothing derived from it travels. False when the Worker predates this field.

capabilities.description: Every capability composed into this Worker, in composition order with the adopter's own app last. A capability absent here has no data to show, which is a fact the client discovers rather than a setting anybody maintains.

items.description: One management operation a connection may perform, as a colon-separated `resource:action` code. The taxonomy is federated: each capability declares its own scopes, and core holds only the seam's.

grantedScopes.description: Every scope this connection holds. Together with each route's own `scope`, this is what tells a client which operations to offer and which to hide.

schema.description: What this Worker is, what it composes, and how to call the admin surface it exposes.

get.summary: Read the connection's key registration state.

200.description: Every key registered against this connection, with its window, and who authorized it for what.

connectionId.description: The connection these keys belong to.

environment.description: The environment that connection is bound to.

keyId.description: The key's id, matched against a token's `kid` header.

kty.description: Key type. Ed25519 is an octet key pair, so this is always `OKP` (RFC 8037).

crv.description: The curve, pinned to Ed25519. Pinned rather than accepted from the key so a weaker curve cannot be smuggled in at registration and honored at verification.

x.description: The base64url-encoded public key point. Public by definition — safe to store, and safe to return from `GET /control-plane/keys`.

publicKey.description: The public key this id names. The private half is never held here.

validFrom.description: When this key became valid, ISO-8601. A call signed before it is rejected.

validUntil.description: When it stops being accepted, ISO-8601, or null while open-ended. Set only by the expire route.

revokedAt.description: When it was revoked outright, ISO-8601, or null. Revocation ignores the window and is immediate.

items.description: One registered public key and its validity window. Two live at once during a rotation overlap.

keys.description: Every registered key, expired and revoked ones included.

authorizedBy.description: Who sanctioned this connection — the signed-in session's email at registration. Null for a connection registered before principals were recorded; absent from a Worker older than the field.

anyOf.description: The email address of the person who sanctioned this connection, read from their signed-in Cloudflare session at registration. Never typed, so never asserted.

actorKind.description: What kind of client this connection is for: `agent`, `dashboard` or `script`. Null for a connection registered before it was recorded; absent from an older Worker.

anyOf.description: What kind of client a connection is for: `agent` (an automated client acting on its own judgment, often unattended), `dashboard` (a management dashboard a person drives, registered through the device-code flow), or `script` (an operator's own automation, doing one fixed thing).

purpose.description: What the client is for, in the registering operator's words. Untrusted text: render it escaped. Null for a connection registered before it was recorded; absent from an older Worker.

anyOf.description: What this connection's client is for, in the registering operator's words — one line of plain text, 200 characters at most, with no control, bidi or invisible characters. Written by a customer and rendered elsewhere, so validated at the boundary.

schema.description: Every key registered against this connection, with its window, and who authorized it for what.

post.summary: Register a key for the connection.

requestBody.description: A request to append one public key to this connection. Appends only: it never touches an existing key's validity, which is what makes a failed rotation harmless.

keyId.description: The new key's id, which a later token names in its `kid` header. Must not already be registered.

kty.description: Key type. Ed25519 is an octet key pair, so this is always `OKP` (RFC 8037).

crv.description: The curve, pinned to Ed25519. Pinned rather than accepted from the key so a weaker curve cannot be smuggled in at registration and honored at verification.

x.description: The base64url-encoded public key point. Public by definition — safe to store, and safe to return from `GET /control-plane/keys`.

publicKey.description: The Ed25519 public key to trust. Only the public half ever crosses the wire — the management client keeps the private key and the adopter never holds anything worth stealing.

schema.description: A request to append one public key to this connection. Appends only: it never touches an existing key's validity, which is what makes a failed rotation harmless.

201.description: The registered key, and the set it joined.

validFrom.description: When its window opened, ISO-8601 — now, by construction.

keyId.description: The key's id, matched against a token's `kid` header.

kty.description: Key type. Ed25519 is an octet key pair, so this is always `OKP` (RFC 8037).

crv.description: The curve, pinned to Ed25519. Pinned rather than accepted from the key so a weaker curve cannot be smuggled in at registration and honored at verification.

publicKey.description: The public key this id names. The private half is never held here.

validFrom.description: When this key became valid, ISO-8601. A call signed before it is rejected.

items.description: One registered public key and its validity window. Two live at once during a rotation overlap.

keys.description: The connection's keys after the append and the prune, so a client sees what it now holds.

schema.description: The registered key, and the set it joined.

post.summary: Retire a superseded key.
post.description: Must be signed with the successor it names as proven.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description: The key to give an end date. Bounded but unconstrained in shape — an unknown id answers 404, not 400.

requestBody.description: A request to expire one superseded key. The successor must be named and must already be live — append, verify, then expire, never replace.

provenKeyId.description: The replacement key that has already been proven against a live `ping`. Required, and checked to be currently active: expiring a key without naming a working successor is the one failure mode with no recovery path, so the route refuses rather than trusting the caller to have checked.

schema.description: A request to expire one superseded key. The successor must be named and must already be live — append, verify, then expire, never replace.

200.description: The expired key, and the set it left behind.

keyId.description: The key just given an end date.

validUntil.description: When its window closed, ISO-8601 — now, by construction.

keyId.description: The key's id, matched against a token's `kid` header.

kty.description: Key type. Ed25519 is an octet key pair, so this is always `OKP` (RFC 8037).

crv.description: The curve, pinned to Ed25519. Pinned rather than accepted from the key so a weaker curve cannot be smuggled in at registration and honored at verification.

x.description: The base64url-encoded public key point. Public by definition — safe to store, and safe to return from `GET /control-plane/keys`.

validUntil.description: When it stops being accepted, ISO-8601, or null while open-ended. Set only by the expire route.

revokedAt.description: When it was revoked outright, ISO-8601, or null. Revocation ignores the window and is immediate.

keys.description: The connection's keys after the expiry.

get.summary: Report where each database this Worker binds stands.
get.description: Applied, pending and undeclared migrations per database, each naming its namespace, and the last group with whether it is still reversible. Undeclared is relative to this Worker: a database shared with another Worker lists that Worker's migrations there. Read-only.

200.description: What is applied, pending and undeclared in each bound database, and which run put it there.

environment.description: The environment this Worker answers for.

state.description: This database's ledger was read.

database.description: The database name, as capabilities declare it in `databases`.

binding.description: The D1 binding it is read through, as `wrangler.jsonc` declares it.

name.description: The composed migration name, exactly as the ledger records it: `0250_audit_0001_init`.

namespace.description: The capability this migration belongs to — its name, as `capabilities[]` in the manifest reports it. Null only for an undeclared migration whose name no Pithy registry could have composed.

items.description: One migration, and the capability namespace it belongs to.

applied.description: Every applied migration, in the order the ledger applied them.

name.description: The composed migration name, exactly as the ledger records it: `0250_audit_0001_init`.

namespace.description: The capability this migration belongs to — its name, as `capabilities[]` in the manifest reports it. Null only for an undeclared migration whose name no Pithy registry could have composed.

items.description: One migration, and the capability namespace it belongs to.

pending.description: Declared by this build and not applied here, in the order they would run.

name.description: The composed migration name, exactly as the ledger records it: `0250_audit_0001_init`.

namespace.description: The capability this migration belongs to — its name, as `capabilities[]` in the manifest reports it. Null only for an undeclared migration whose name no Pithy registry could have composed.

items.description: One migration, and the capability namespace it belongs to.

undeclared.description: Applied here and not declared by this Worker, sorted. Relative to this Worker: a database shared with another Worker lists that Worker's migrations here. Otherwise Kysely reads one as a corrupted chain and applies nothing.

group.description: The group's value: the `--group` the run was given, or the ISO-8601 timestamp it generated.

appliedAt.description: When this group last applied something here, ISO-8601.

name.description: The composed migration name, exactly as the ledger records it: `0250_audit_0001_init`.

namespace.description: The capability this migration belongs to — its name, as `capabilities[]` in the manifest reports it. Null only for an undeclared migration whose name no Pithy registry could have composed.

items.description: One migration, and the capability namespace it belongs to.

migrations.description: What this group applied in this database and is still applied, in application order.

state.description: The group's migrations are the contiguous tip of this database's chain. Not a promise that `pithy migrate --rollback --group <value>` runs: the CLI also refuses an undeclared migration in the ledger, and keeps back or refuses a database another environment binds.

oneOf.description: A group nothing on this database's ledger sits over.

state.description: Something sits over the group or inside it, so reversing it by name is refused.

above.description: The groups in the way, newest first.

name.description: The composed migration name, exactly as the ledger records it: `0250_audit_0001_init`.

namespace.description: The capability this migration belongs to — its name, as `capabilities[]` in the manifest reports it. Null only for an undeclared migration whose name no Pithy registry could have composed.

items.description: One migration, and the capability namespace it belongs to.

ungrouped.description: The migrations in the way that no group claims, newest first. Nothing can be reversed by group while one of them is at the tip.

oneOf.description: A group with something in its way, and what that is.

position.description: Whether the group is the top of the chain, or what is in its way.

anyOf.description: The newest group with anything still applied in this database.

lastGroup.description: The newest group with anything applied here, or null when nothing applied here was ever grouped.

oneOf.description: A database whose ledger was read.

state.description: This database's ledger could not be read on this call.

database.description: The database name, as capabilities declare it in `databases`.

binding.description: The D1 binding it would be read through.

oneOf.description: A database that could not be read. No lists, so nothing about it reads as zero. The other databases still answer.

items.description: One database this Worker binds: its migration state, or the fact that it could not be read.

databases.description: One entry per database this Worker binds, sorted by database name. One unreadable costs only itself.

schema.description: What is applied, pending and undeclared in each bound database, and which run put it there.

get.summary: Report every stored field marked with a privacy class.
get.description: Every D1 table and KV store this Worker composed that holds a privacy-marked field, with each field's path, its class and where it is stored, beside the declared-and-observed posture. Derived at runtime from the deployed schemas. Read-only.

200.description: Every schema this Worker stores that holds a marked field, each field's path and class, and where it lives.

environment.description: The environment this Worker answers for.

items.description: A class name.

declared.description: The classes the project declared, as attested by the last `pithy deploy`. Empty when it declared none; null when no attestation reached this Worker.

items.description: A class name.

observed.description: Every class with at least one marked field in this Worker's storage schemas, derived at runtime. Null when the project declared no class, because nothing was walked.

counts.description: Marked fields per observed class. A class with none is absent rather than zero. Null when nothing was walked.

items.description: A class name.

observedNotDeclared.description: Classes the code holds that the project never declared — a posture change nobody escalated. Null when nothing was walked.

items.description: A class name.

declaredNotObserved.description: Classes declared with no marked field behind them — an unfinished migration. Null when nothing was walked.

consoleGate.description: The console gate, as last attested.

consoleGateReason.description: Why the gate is `unverifiable`, in one sentence. Null otherwise.

attestedAt.description: When the attestation was written, ISO-8601, or null when there is none. A version created long after it is a build the attestation does not describe.

items.description: A storage kind: `d1` tables, or `kv` stores.

sources.description: The storage the observed classes were derived from. Anything not listed was not walked; empty when nothing was.

retirement.description: The field key's retirement guard (#390): whether a version due to leave is held live, and by what. Absent on a Worker whose core predates encrypted fields.

blocked.description: Whether a version due to leave the window is being held live by one of `reasons`.

items.description: `unrotatable` — an encrypted field rests outside D1, so nothing can prove it re-sealed. `incomplete-coverage` — a schema source the guard derives from was not read. `stale` — a row still holds an envelope or an index under a version due to leave.

reasons.description: Every reason the guard is not clean now, empty when it is. Read directly: never inferred.

liveVersions.description: How many field-key versions are live. Two is the normal state: current and previous.

posture.description: The declared and observed classes, the delta, and the console gate.

schemasWalked.description: How many storage schemas were walked, marked or not, across the sources `posture.sources` names.

capability.description: The capability that declared the schema, as the manifest's `capabilities[]` names it.

storage.description: Where it is stored: a `d1` table or a `kv` store.

container.description: The D1 database name or the KV namespace name it lives in.

name.description: The table name, or the KV store name.

path.description: Where the field sits. A D1 column path (`email`, `address.line1`, `profile.phone` inside a JSON column), or a KV entry's part first (`key.email`, `value.token`, `metadata.ip`, or `value` for a whole marked value). An array element is `[]`, a record's value `*`.

class.description: The privacy class it is marked with: `secret`, `pii`, `phi`, `pci`, or an adopter's own.

truncated.description: Set where the class is assumed rather than found: a read ran out of its budget there, or the schema could not be read at all, so any class may be marked below it. Absent where the schema was read to the end.

sameAs.description: Set on a reference: the path this field's position was first listed under, once the list reached its cap on paths. The class is marked somewhere beneath both, and the paths beneath this one are those beneath that one.

encryptedAtRest.description: Whether the field rests encrypted (#390). Absent where the core cannot say — an assumed class, a reference, or a core older than encrypted fields — and never defaulted to false.

unrotatable.description: Set on an encrypted field whose storage is not D1: it can never be rotated, and it blocks retirement.

items.description: One marked field and its class.

fields.description: Every marked field in it, in schema order.

encrypted.description: Every field marked encrypted at rest, classed or not (#390). Absent on a Worker whose core predates encrypted fields.

path.description: Where the encrypted field sits, on the same paths as `fields[].path`.

unrotatable.description: Set where the storage is not D1, so the field can never be rotated.

items.description: One encrypted field.
One storage schema and the marked fields it holds.

schemas.description: Every schema holding a marked field, in composition order. A schema with none is not listed.

schema.description: Every schema this Worker stores that holds a marked field, each field's path and class, and where it lives.

get.summary: Read the status of every declared secret, never a value.

200.description: The status of every declared secret, and any whose stored rows would not decode.

name.description: The secret's registry name.

backend.description: Where the value lives. Decides what a null `createdAt` means.

valueType.description: How the value is interpreted: `text` or `json`.

rotatable.description: Whether a value-rotator may manage it. Never changes what is reported.

kind.description: Replaced by producing a new value the same way it was minted. Every `origin.kind: "minted"` secret, and nothing else — if the kit can make one it can make another.

oneOf.description: Rotated by the kit, on its own. The tag carries everything; there is nobody to call.

kind.description: Replaced by calling the issuer, which returns the new value. The kit cannot invent this call; the capability or the adopter supplies it, and it changes state in somebody else's system.

documentation.description: What the call does, for an operator deciding whether to trust it with a live credential.

oneOf.description: Rotated by calling the issuer. The new value comes back from somebody else's system.

kind.description: A human, in a console. No API returns the new value — a GitHub or Google OAuth client secret. This is a real answer, not a missing one.

documentation.description: The page where it is done.

oneOf.description: Rotated by a human, in a console. A real answer, and the page is the whole help.

anyOf.description: How this secret is replaced, declared separately from `origin` because neither follows from the other: a GitLab token is `obtained` and rotates by `provider`, while an OAuth client secret is `obtained` and rotates only by `manual`. Declared per secret, never per issuer — some Cloudflare secrets roll and some do not.

rotation.description: How this secret is replaced: `local`, `provider`, or `manual` — with the issuer, and the page a human goes to. Null when the registry declares nothing, which is not the same as `manual`. **This is the field a client branches on to decide whether a rotation control exists at all**, and it is metadata by construction: a kind, an issuer and an `https:` documentation URL are all it can hold. An issuer this client has never heard of parses as `other` rather than failing, so a Worker newer than its reader still renders.

keyVersion.description: Which master-key version the stored envelope sits under, or null when nothing is stored here.

createdAt.description: When it was first written to this store, ISO-8601; null when it is not stored here.

updatedAt.description: When its value was last written, ISO-8601; null when it is not stored here.

at.description: When the failed attempt closed, ISO-8601.

anyOf.description: Why a rotation row closed failed, as a code. `roll-failed`, `not-recorded` and `not-rotated` are a value rotation's. `at-rest-incomplete` and `at-rest-unconfirmed` are the whole-store master-key rotation's. `not-retired` is an unattended value rotation that landed and kept the previous version, because a value sealed under it at rest was not re-encrypted. `field-key-overdue` is a field-key version still live when the next rotation came due, `field-key-ceiling` a rotation refused at four live versions, `field-key-unconfirmed` a field-key write the binding never showed, and `field-key-incomplete` a field-key pass that did not finish (#390).

items.description: One secret's status as a client reads it. Metadata only — this shape cannot express a value.

secrets.description: Every named secret the composed Worker declares, by name. Keyed entries are excluded.

unreadable.description: Declared secrets whose stored rows would not decode, by registry name — so one bad row costs its own entry and names itself, instead of costing the read (#387). Carries no reason; why a row is malformed is a question for the database, not for a client.

anyOf.description: Why a rotation row closed failed, as a code. `roll-failed`, `not-recorded` and `not-rotated` are a value rotation's. `at-rest-incomplete` and `at-rest-unconfirmed` are the whole-store master-key rotation's. `not-retired` is an unattended value rotation that landed and kept the previous version, because a value sealed under it at rest was not re-encrypted. `field-key-overdue` is a field-key version still live when the next rotation came due, `field-key-ceiling` a rotation refused at four live versions, `field-key-unconfirmed` a field-key write the binding never showed, and `field-key-incomplete` a field-key pass that did not finish (#390).

kind.description: How the registry says this secret is replaced — the same fact `rotation.kind` reports on a status read.

rolled.description: Whether the issuer's credential was actually replaced. True only for a `provider` rotation that reached its rotator; a `local` mint rolls nothing anywhere.

rollFailed.description: Whether the **rotator itself** threw, rather than the store after it. With `rolled`, this is the difference between *was rolled* and *may have been rolled*: a call that reached the issuer and lost its answer cannot be told from one that never landed, and a report claiming either is wrong half the time about the fact being acted on. attempts.description: How many store attempts the failing environment cost. Null when nothing was stored.

rotation.description: The outcome. One secret per call, so there is no summary line to hide a partial failure behind.

id.description: The matching record's id.

filename.description: The original client filename, including extension.

contentType.description: The MIME type of the stored bytes.

size.description: The object's size in bytes, or null while it is not known.

ownerId.description: The user who owns the record. Null for a system-owned record, and for any record read by someone not acting for its organization; absent from a Worker that predates it.

get.summary: Count media held, per organization or per owner.
get.description: Stored records and their bytes. A per-owner read names its organization, so no figure ever spans two.

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: `organization` is one row per organization; `owner` is one row per owner within the organization named, never across organizations.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: Restrict to one organization. Required with `groupBy=owner` and with `ownerId`, because a per-owner figure is only ever an organization's. `none` is the records written with no organization in force.

parameters.name: ownerId
parameters.description: Restrict to one owner, within the organization named.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Count records created at or after this instant, ISO-8601.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Count records created before this instant, ISO-8601.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most rows to return. 100 by default.

bytes.description: Their total size in bytes. A record of unknown size counts zero.

items.description: Records and bytes held by one organization, or by one owner within one organization.

rows.description: Largest first. Capped at the requested limit.

truncated.description: Whether more rows matched than were returned.

schema.description: Records and bytes held, grouped as asked.

effectiveAt.description: When it happens, ISO-8601. On a scheduled cancellation this is the date the customer is owed — it is where 'until' comes from once the next billing date has gone blank.

resumesAt.description: When a paused subscription comes back, ISO-8601, when the store named a day. Null on a pause means indefinitely; null on a cancel or a resume means the field does not apply.

anyOf.description: A change the store will apply at a stated future moment, on a subscription that is fine until then.

scheduledChange.description: The change waiting to land, or null when nothing is. The only field that separates a subscription ending this period from one renewing.

kind.description: What happens next — a renewal falling due, or the scheduled change landing.

oneOf.description: Something is going to happen, and the store said when.

kind.description: Nothing is scheduled and nothing is due. An expired subscription and one whose store went quiet both land here, and neither of them renews.

at.description: There is no date, because there is no event.

nextEvent.description: What happens next and when, already resolved — the scheduled change ahead of the billing date. The sentence a screen prints.

percent.description: How many percent off, 0 exclusive to 100 inclusive. 100 is a comped period, which is legal.

oneOf.description: A single period's discount — a launch offer on the first invoice.

kind.description: Every period, for as long as the subscription runs.

oneOf.description: A permanent rate. Nothing lapses, so nothing surprises anyone later.

kind.description: A fixed number of billing periods, then list price.

billingPeriods.description: How many billing periods the discount applies to, counted the way a customer counts renewals. Twelve on a monthly plan is a year; twelve on an annual plan is twelve years.

oneOf.description: A rate that lapses — the one whose end date a customer must be told about.

duration.description: How long it lasts, in billing periods.

billingInterval.description: How often the plan renews. Required when `duration` is `repeating`, and refused otherwise — a duration that does not lapse has nothing to count.

maxRedemptions.description: How many times the code may be claimed in total, or omit for unlimited. It guards the customer path and only the customer path: the store counts a redemption when a checkout or a transaction uses the code and refuses the next one past the limit, and it holds when a webhook never arrives because the count is the store's rather than ours. It does not guard an administrative application against an existing subscription. Measured against the Paddle sandbox on 2026-08-14: a code with `usage_limit: 1` was applied to two subscriptions with `times_used` still `0`, went to `1` only when a transaction billed under it completed, and refused the next transaction after that. Stripe and Lemon Squeezy are unmeasured, so assume the same of them. So a staff comp applied by updating a subscription is not stopped here, and an adopter's own record of who was offered a code is the only thing that would stop it.

redeemableUntil.description: After this moment the code can no longer be *claimed*. It does not end a discount already applied: a customer who redeemed it yesterday keeps their rate for its full duration. Named for that meaning because the providers' own fields do not agree on it, and a fixture pins each rail against a code already redeemed.

get.summary: List the support inbox.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: `true` for the done pile, `false` or absent for the open inbox — which is the default on purpose.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter to one category — what the classifier made of it.

parameters.name: declaredCategory
parameters.description: Filter to one category **the submitter chose**, which is a different question from `category` and answers it about different threads. Combining the two is how an operator finds the disagreements; asking for this one alone is how they triage a project with `ai.enabled: false`, where nothing ever writes the other.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Filter to one priority.

parameters.name: sentiment
parameters.description: Filter to one sentiment.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Filter to one channel — `email` for mail, `app` for what signed-in users filed from inside the app. Absent shows both, which is the right default for an inbox that is one queue however things arrived.

parameters.name: inbox
parameters.description: Filter to one configured inbox address, for a Worker serving several.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text over subjects and bodies. Keyword search — the words people actually remember.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to resume, from the previous page's `nextCursor`. Opaque; a malformed one is a first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many threads to return. Bounded, because a verified client can still have a bug.

200.description: A page of the inbox, as one viewer sees it.

id.description: The thread's UUID — what every other route on this surface takes.

channel.description: How this conversation started — `email` at an inbound address, or `app` from a signed-in user of the adopter's own app.

inboxAddress.description: The support address this thread arrived on, lowercased, and the address a reply comes back to. Null only on an `app` thread in a project with no inbound address configured.

subject.description: The subject of the message that opened the thread. Later replies never rewrite it.

fromName.description: The sender's display name, or null. Untrusted text; render it escaped.

senderAuthenticated.description: Whether the sender was proved to be who they claim. On `email` that means the `From:` header was proved, and false means unproven rather than forged — it is what withholds the customer link. Always true on `app`, where a session proved it before the request arrived.

userId.description: The user this sender resolves to, or null when nobody or unproven.

anyOf.description: How this thread's `userId` was established: `session` means an authenticated request proved it, `email_address` means it was matched from the address in a `From:` header. Never equivalent — one is the identity, the other is a lookup on a claim.

accountLinkSource.description: How `userId` was established, or null when there is no link. **Render these differently.** `session` means an authenticated request proved it and the account *is* the caller; `email_address` means it was matched against an address in a header nobody proved. The same operator action — a refund, a reset — follows from very different evidence.

declaredCategory.description: **What the submitter said this is about**, or null when nobody said — every mail thread, and every app thread filed without a chooser. **Render this and `category` differently, and never fold one into the other.** They are two facts with two authors: this is a claim by the person writing, `category` is a machine's judgment about them, and an operator deciding what to do needs to know which is on screen. Where they disagree, that disagreement is the most useful thing on the row. Where `classifiedAt` is null this is the only category anybody stated.

category.description: **What the classifier made of it** — the current category key, from this project's own federated taxonomy. `uncategorized` until a classification lands, and forever on a project with `ai.enabled: false`.

priority.description: How fast this thread needs a human.

sentiment.description: How the sender sounds — the churn signal.

confidence.description: The model's confidence in the current classification, or null until one lands.

model.description: The Workers AI model that produced the classification, or null.

classifiedAt.description: When the classification was written, ISO-8601; null until it is.

archived.description: Done. One shared boolean, not per viewer.

archivedAt.description: When it was last archived, ISO-8601; null while open.

archivedBy.description: The control-plane subject that archived it, for convenience only — the answer to 'who marked this done' comes from the audit trail.

messageCount.description: How many messages the thread holds, inbound and outbound together.

lastMessageAt.description: When the thread last moved, ISO-8601. The inbox sorts on this.

createdAt.description: When the thread row was created, ISO-8601.

updatedAt.description: When the thread row was last written, ISO-8601.

read.description: Whether this viewer has read it. False when they have no flag row, the common case.

snoozedUntil.description: When this viewer's snooze expires, ISO-8601, or null.

items.description: One conversation in the inbox, carrying the calling viewer's own read and snooze state.

nextCursor.description: Where the next page resumes. Null at the end of the list. Opaque — pass it back verbatim.

post.summary: Write in to support from the app.

requestBody.description: An in-app support request from a signed-in user: what it is about, what happened, and what it carries.

subject.description: What the request is about. Becomes the thread's name in the inbox and the subject of every reply.

body.description: The report itself, as the person wrote it. Plain text — it is prose, never markup.

declaredCategory.description: What the person writing says this is about, from your app's own chooser. **Named for what it is, on the wire as well as in the row**: a field called `category` here would land in a column of that name that this never touches, which is the exact confusion the two columns exist to prevent. Bounded to a key's shape here and checked against your effective taxonomy in the handler — a key you do not declare is **refused**, because a chooser was built from that taxonomy and a value outside it is the client's bug. Accepted only when opening a request: sent alongside `threadId` it is refused rather than ignored.

threadId.description: Continue this conversation instead of opening one. Accepted only for the caller's **own** app thread; anybody else's answers 404, which is the same answer a thread that does not exist gets — a 403 would confirm the id names a real conversation.

context.description: What the app knows and the user did not type — screen, build, platform, environment, locale. A closed set: an undeclared key is refused rather than stored, so this cannot quietly become a telemetry pipe.

screen.description: Where in the app they were — a route, a screen name, whatever the app calls it. The single most useful field, because it turns 'the button does nothing' into a place to look.

appVersion.description: The build the report came from. Answers 'is this already fixed' without a round trip, which is the whole reason a bug report asks for it.

platform.description: The client the app is running as — `ios`, `android`, `web`, or whatever the adopter's own build calls itself. Free text rather than an enum: the set of clients is the adopter's, not this capability's.

environment.description: Which environment the client was pointed at. A report from staging read as production is a bug hunted in the wrong database, and the client is the only thing that knows.

locale.description: The locale the app was rendering in. Carried because a whole class of reports — a date a day out, a currency in the wrong place, text that overflows — is only reproducible in the reporter's locale. Not validated as a tag here: see `enqueueEmail`, which normalizes it before it reaches a column that is.

attachments.description: Files attached to the request. Bounded by `submission.attachments` in the adopter's config — count, decoded size, and an allowlist of types — and refused as a whole rather than silently trimmed. The ceiling here is the one that holds whatever that config says, and it is checked before any payload is decoded.

filename.description: The filename as the client declares it. **Recorded and never honored** — the R2 key is server-derived, so this is metadata a console renders escaped, not a path anything resolves.
